overview: White fianchettoes the queen's bishop and pushes the b-pawn to b5, gaining queenside space, then supports the centre with e3. Black builds a solid centre with ...d5 and ...c5 or ...Bd6 and aims to undermine the b5 pawn and exploit the lost time. Play is flank-oriented with unbalanced pawns and no early tactics.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Nf3, Be2 and c4 or d4, using the Bb2 on the long diagonal.
Keep the b5 pawn as a space grab and expand with a4 or c4.

black_ideas.idea: Build a solid centre with ...c5, ...Bd6, ...O-O and attack the b5 pawn with ...a6.
Fight for the dark squares and the e4 break.

typical_structures.structure: White pawn on b5 with e3 and d4 or c4; Black central pawns on d5 and e6, flexible.

character.notes: Slow manoeuvring game with a shifted queenside; neither side takes early risks.

soundness.notes: Playable but Black gets a comfortable game; not refuted.

structure.notes: The centre is undecided with flank pawns advanced.

approach.notes: Played by strong players now and then as a surprise but seldom main choice.

level.notes: Needs sound positional judgment, little theory.

character.reason: Slow flank-oriented manoeuvring with no early tactics.

structure.reason: The centre is undecided and flank pawns are advanced.

approach.reason: Polish with 3.b5 is mainly a surprise weapon.

level.reason: Plans are clear but need positional judgment.

plans.reason: White fianchettoes and expands on the queenside.
